purpose: Compare workflow round robin to distributing long first-request message histories across both replicas. Independent Coder-7B processes on both A100s in both conditions, no prefetch or admission cap. The first timing run uses history-based placement and the second uses round robin; repeated deployment order is a limitation. Charge both GPUs throughout each measured wave. Keep the assigned GPU for all dependent turns.
protocol: Online assignment at the first real model submission. Estimate history size using serialized bytes of the received messages, including the current question. Split at 4096 bytes. Choose the replica with fewer assigned workflows in that size class, then fewer total assigned workflows, then lower GPU index. Same single dispatcher and class measurement overhead in both arms. Reset assignment counts after each fully drained wave. Preserve real arrival order under locking. Shuffled waves randomly place four readers using the fixture seed. In imperfect waves also exchange prior history lengths for two reader and two long-tool jobs, keeping their true tool sizes and waits intact. Router never sees the role or future tool result. 30ms offered-arrival grid and 5s/8s/80ms budgets as before.
gate: For each of regular, shuffled, imperfect groups of 32 C16 jobs require no previously valid answers lost, at least as many SLO completions, greater SLO goodput per GPU-hour, reader scheduled-first p95, reader gap p95-of-p95 and overall last content p95 within +5% of round robin. Give per-device mix and all cases, including tradeoffs. An isolated structured traffic win qualifies only for that workload, not general adoption.
